title: PracticePay Patient Financing — Deferred Interest and Promotional Period Schedule
content:
On PracticePay Patient Financing, deferred interest exists only on the two deferred-interest plans. This schedule sets, per plan, whether interest accrued during the promotional period is billed when the plan is not paid in full by the end of the promotional period, how it accrues, when it is billed, the payoff test that forgives it, the reminder before the period ends, and how an open billing dispute bears on the payoff test.

| Plan | Deferred interest billed if not paid in full by the end of the promotional period | Disputed amount left out of the payoff test while the dispute is open | Days after a no-error resolution to pay the disputed amount and still meet the test | Reminder of the payoff amount, days before the end of the promotional period |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PracticePay 6-Month Deferred Interest Plan | yes | yes | 30 | 30 |
| PracticePay 6-Month No Interest Plan | no | no | 0 | 0 |
| PracticePay 12-Month Deferred Interest Plan | yes | yes | 30 | 60 |
| PracticePay 12-Month No Interest Plan | no | no | 0 | 0 |
| PracticePay 24-Month Reduced APR Plan | no | no | 0 | 0 |
| PracticePay 48-Month Reduced APR Plan | no | no | 0 | 0 |
| PracticePay 60-Month Extended Plan | no | no | 0 | 0 |

## The deferred-interest terms of the two deferred-interest plans

Both the PracticePay 6-Month Deferred Interest Plan and the PracticePay 12-Month Deferred Interest Plan carry these terms; on every other plan each of them is not applicable.

- **How deferred interest accrues:** simple daily interest at the plan APR on the plan balance excluding fees, from the purchase date, posted to the memo at each statement closing.
- **When unpaid-promotion deferred interest is billed:** the day after the end date of the promotional period.
- **Test for forgiving deferred interest:** the plan balance, less amounts under open billing disputes, is 0.00 at the end of the end date of the promotional period.

All day counts in this schedule are calendar days.

## Points of reading

- The reminder is sent 30 calendar days before the end of the promotional period on the 6-month deferred-interest plan and 60 calendar days before it on the 12-month deferred-interest plan; the other plans send none.
- The no-interest plans have a promotional period but no deferred interest: nothing accrues to a memo and nothing is billed when their promotional period ends.
